worked_solution:
If we let $u=7-2x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2\,⟹\,-\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $5$ | $3$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{3}^{7-2x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{5}^{3}{3}^{u}(-\frac{1}{2})\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{5}^{3}{3}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{3}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}){|}_{5}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}({3}^{3}-{3}^{5}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(27-243) \\  & =\frac{108}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$
